rules.summary: Inside backend/domains one sub-domain must not read or write another sub-domain's underscore-prefixed members or call its private methods. Such access bypasses the anti-corruption seam, so a refactor in one domain silently breaks another; interaction must go through public contract methods, DTO payloads or EventBus events.
rules.title: Cross-domain private member access ban

rules.summary: Business thresholds, enums, copy text and numeric values must be read through GameConfig.get_int, get_float or get_string with an explicit safe default; a bare get_value() call outside the facade returns an untyped Variant and is a violation. Untyped reads hide the real source of truth and defeat configuration reload.
rules.title: GameConfig-only configuration reads

rules.summary: Configuration tables whose key-order independent digest matches another table form a duplicate group and must be reconciled against the uniqueness manifest before they may coexist. An unregistered duplicate group becomes two competing sources of truth; the engine only reports the group and never rewrites the tables itself.
rules.title: Duplicate configuration table detection

rules.summary: A pure domain model or solver must extend RefCounted or Object; extending Node, Node2D, Control or any other scene-tree type couples domain logic to render-tree lifetime and blocks headless testing. Presentation interaction must travel through EventBus broadcasts or DTO arguments.
rules.title: Domain model scene-tree decoupling

rules.summary: A channel must be shaped <domain_id>.<event_name> where the first segment is an id already registered as a game domain, and channel values must come from the channel registry rather than scattered bare strings. An unregistered prefix such as auth or hud breaks routing and leaves the event untraceable.
rules.title: EventBus channel naming convention

rules.summary: Every channel event_name must have a matching template key in that domain's narrative table unless the channel is declared as purely structured. A missing key silently drops the user-visible copy at run time while the event itself still dispatches, so the defect surfaces only as blank text.
rules.title: Channel narrative key alignment

rules.summary: The ids registered in the event bus channel registry must equal the EventChannelDefinition constant values. Any difference means two sources of truth, so the publisher and the subscriber stop agreeing on the same channel.
rules.title: Channel registry single source alignment

rules.summary: A literal payload passed to emit_domain_event must carry the fields the narrative renderer needs to fill its template; a purely structured event may omit them but must declare that explicitly. An incomplete payload renders as empty or colourless narrative text.
rules.title: Broadcast payload narrative completeness

rules.summary: In GDScript 4 a lambda captures built-in typed locals by value and captured objects can form reference cycles, so assigning to a captured primitive inside the closure never updates the outer variable. Mutable state must travel through a Callable or a RefCounted holder object.
rules.title: Lambda capture lifetime safety

rules.summary: Class and enum names must be PascalCase, variables, functions and parameters snake_case, constants UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, private members underscore-prefixed, and static var must never be UPPER_SNAKE. One scheme across the code base keeps a symbol's kind predictable from its spelling alone.
rules.title: Unified identifier naming scheme

rules.summary: A class that enters ObjectPool must implement reset_state() and be fully reset when borrowed, and ownership must be validated on return to reject a double return. Residual state leaks into the next borrower and a double return corrupts pool bookkeeping.
rules.title: Object pool lifecycle contract

rules.summary: A loop body must not re-read GameConfig.get_* each iteration, rebuild the same string every pass, or run a linear Array.find() scan. Cache the value or build a Dictionary index before entering the loop, because per-iteration repeated work multiplies straight into the frame budget on a hot path.
rules.title: Zero repeated work inside loops

rules.summary: A per-frame or high-frequency loop body must not call .new() or .duplicate(true) on every iteration; bounded low-frequency paths such as turn-level, event-driven or load-time code are exempt once the magnitude bound is documented in a comment. Per-iteration allocation causes garbage collection pauses and memory fragmentation.
rules.title: No transient heap allocation in hot loops

rules.summary: A loop must not run percent placeholders or string formatting per iteration; precompile the template or assemble the text from a lookup table. Each iteration otherwise allocates a transient String and re-parses the format pattern.
rules.title: Loop string formatting elimination

rules.summary: A loop must not locate items with Array.find() or repeated containment scans; build a Dictionary hash index during setup. Linear scanning makes the surrounding loop cost O(N) per lookup instead of O(1).
rules.title: Loop linear search elimination

rules.summary: Calling the Godot globals randf(), randi(), randomize(), randf_range(), randi_range() or randfn() is a violation; randomness must be drawn through DeterministicRNG with a controlled seed. Unseeded global randomness makes replays, arbitration and defect reproduction non-repeatable.
rules.title: Deterministic random dispatch only

rules.summary: Arguments passed to emit_signal() or signal.emit() must match the signal declaration in count and type, and a bare null must not be emitted into a typed parameter. A mismatch crashes or silently corrupts the receiving side.
rules.title: Signal emission argument contract

rules.summary: Property variables must declare an explicit type, and local variables must use := inference or declare a type rather than a bare untyped var. An untyped declaration lets a wrong value type travel silently until it fails far from its origin.
rules.title: Explicit typing and static inference

rules.summary: Every business function must annotate each parameter type and declare its return type, using -> void when nothing is returned; bare parameters or a missing return annotation are violations. An unannotated signature cannot be statically checked, so type defects surface only at run time.
rules.title: Function signature type completeness

rules.summary: A := binding must not be applied to a dictionary get(), pop_front() or pop_back() result that may be null or Variant, because inference then hides the type defect. Declare the expected type with an explicit default and guard it, since this is exactly where a null slips past the compiler.
rules.title: No blind inference from dynamic returns

rules.summary: A presentation node must not redraw on every single property change; mark the state dirty and flush the redraw once per frame through a deferred call. Redrawing per mutation multiplies layout work inside one frame and drops frames.
rules.title: Batched presentation redraw

rules.summary: Analyzer threw an unhandled exception on a single file (escalates to error if failOnAnalyzerError is set).
Over-abstraction and redundant indirection: introducing cross-layer forwardingtrampolines, inverted dependencies, or cycles for trivial commonalities.
File boundary imbalance: multiple high-complexity functions in a single file lacksemantic cohesion, abnormally aggregating responsibilities.
Cross-domain internal penetration: bypassing public export facade contracts to directly access private internal implementations.
Environment configuration leak: pure domain models directly read environment variables or disk configuration files.
Declared configuration property is never referenced in decisions, control flow, orcalculations across the codebase (dead configuration).
Duplicate configuration entries declared across multiple locations, violating single source of truth.
Implicit configuration scatter: business code directly reads environment variables or tuning constants.
Unstructured configuration access: accessing configuration in an unstructured,arbitrary manner across layers without a centralized registry.
Configuration tightly coupled with domain logic: domain models directly bind tospecific config file formats or disk parsers.
Configuration over-abstraction: simple static configuration introduces excessiveunnecessary indirection and forwarding layers.
Flat configuration sprawl antipattern: large volume of configuration files sprawledacross root directory without domain isomorphic hierarchy.
Configuration sub-table routing contract breach: unregistered sub-table detached fromcore routing contract, lacking dot-notation routing.
Polyglot AST parsing and adapter logic must be decoupled into independent adaptermodules; analyzer core must not mix AST construction details.
Core reverse flow: domain layer inversely depends on outer application, infrastructure, or interface layers.
Layer bypass: interface layer controllers bypass application services to directly couple with infrastructure implementations.
Formal layering illusion: directory structure appears separated, but call graphs and data flows violate layer boundaries.
Monolithic dispatchers with excessive branches (> 8) tightly couple domain logic, violating the Open-Closed Principle.
Dispatcher closure fragmentation: Object literal defines excessive inline function closures (>= 15), causing closure explosion and function inflation.
Hollow facade payload and insufficient density: facade module lacks substantive domainorchestration, schema validation, or immutability contracts.
Implicit global mutable state: modules are tightly coupled via top-level global variables or static singletons.
Headless architecture breach: core business logic or calculation modules directly bind to UI/IDE view frameworks.
Responsibility leak: pure domain models directly reference or leak external frameworks (Express, Vue, Godot, ORM).
Layer boundary breach: outer implementations are directly referenced by inner layers (Clean/DDD inverted hierarchy).
Plumbing overhead ratio (POR) exceeds threshold; wiring code dominates logic payload.
File entity role imbalance and pseudo-shared library: file carries excessive mutablestate or coupled logic but is heavily imported as a shared library.
Business module harboring unbounded common capabilities: domain module internally hostsand exports general infrastructure or utilities.
Strategy skeleton candidate: detected complex workflows sharing isomorphicpre-validation and post-execution teardown steps.
Monolithic template renderer coupling: oversized function concatenates deep HTML/SVG/DSL templates without subcomponent decomposition.
Kitchen-sink utility antipattern: detected utils/common dumping ground file accumulatingheterogeneous unstructured logic.
Dynamic namespace for adapter-mapped external findings
rules.title: Dynamic namespace for adapter-mapped external findings

rules.summary: The art delivery contract lists the audio asset category with the Ogg container as its required format, alongside 32-bit PNG textures and TTF or OTF fonts. A delivery in an unlisted container cannot be imported by the asset pipeline, so the ticket cannot close.
rules.title: Audio delivery container format

rules.summary: The art delivery contract lists the icon asset category against a legibility definition of done: contrast at or above 4.5:1 against the #0F131A dark base, and no smearing or clumping when scaled down to 16px. An icon that fails either check is unreadable in dense list and slot layouts.
rules.title: Icon legibility acceptance baseline

rules.summary: Universal containers ship as four nine-patch specifications with fixed per-file slice margins: 128x128 panel at 16px, 64x64 card at 8px, 96x96 modal at 12px and 32x32 tooltip at 4px. Fixed slice margins keep corners and borders undistorted across each file's supported size range.
rules.title: Nine-patch container four-spec slicing

rules.summary: Each of the Primary, Secondary, Danger and Flat variants ships four state slices, normal, hover, pressed and disabled, for sixteen files at 48x48 with 6px slice margins and 4px corner radius; the pressed slice shifts content down 1px and drops its 2px drop shadow to 0. A missing state forces the engine to reuse normal and erases press feedback.
rules.title: Button variant state matrix

rules.summary: A slot is five stacked 48x48 layers rather than one flat image: recess base, centred 32x32 icon, 2px quality frame whose centre 44x44 stays fully transparent, state overlay, and a count badge anchored bottom-right. Separating frame and badge from the icon is what lets one icon serve every tier and stack count.
rules.title: Five-layer slot assembly

rules.summary: Bars are built from a 64x16 track sliced 4px left and right, a 64x16 fill sliced 2px each side, and a pure white 60 percent opacity damage buffer layer beneath the fill; bar height is restricted to 16px or 20px and stretched horizontally only. Mixing arbitrary heights or vertical slices breaks alignment across HP, MP, AP and experience bars.
rules.title: Meter skin three-layer suite

rules.summary: Status dots are 16x16 circles with one colour each for error, warning and info; rarity tags are 60x20 plates with 2px corner radius at 25 percent opacity carrying a 1px quality-coloured left rule; dividers are a 256x2 fading line plus an 8x8 centre stud. Without these fixed micro-sizes the badge, tag and divider components cannot be shared across views.
rules.title: Badge tag and divider micro-assets

rules.summary: The eight economic assets, three coin tiers, four mana crystal grades and rations, ship at both 16x16 and 32x32 with a 1px dark anti-aliasing shadow ring, each mapped to one backend economy field. Dual resolution keeps the top-bar strip crisp without a separately downscaled variant per layout.
rules.title: Currency icon dual resolution set

rules.summary: Vital, buff and debuff glyphs are all 24x24 black 1px outline silhouettes so they stay legible on any bar colour or dark background. A glyph that adds fill detail disappears against the dark UI and leaves the player unable to tell a buff from a debuff.
rules.title: Vital and affliction glyph style

rules.summary: The eight named HUD navigation icons are 24x24 clean cool-silver line art at #A0AEC0 with a gold #ECC94B highlight across the whole glyph on hover, each mapped to one of the eight named navigation entries. A different line weight makes one entry read as belonging to another system.
rules.title: Navigation icon line style

rules.summary: Item icons ship as visual category archetypes on a 48x48 canvas with the silhouette confined to 32x32 and 8px padding, carrying no frame and no outer glow. Because tier frame and count come from the slot layers, one archetype icon serves every item sharing that shape and function.
rules.title: Category archetype slot icons

rules.summary: Ten 48x48 transparent PNG verb icons are required, each encoding one physical motion, with explicit trajectory angles where the specification fixes them: stab at 0 degrees, parry at 15 degrees, hack at 30 degrees, lift at 45 degrees and chop at 90 degrees. A verb icon whose motion angle contradicts its action reads as the wrong move during combat.
rules.title: Physical verb icon set

rules.summary: Six 48x48 transparent PNG runes are required, one per elemental archetype, each drawn as an arcane vector mark. Binding one rune per archetype keeps a newly authored spell on the existing art slot instead of requiring a bespoke icon.
rules.title: Elemental rune archetype set

rules.summary: Story relic assets are RGBA 32-bit transparent PNG on a 48x48 canvas with the core silhouette confined to 36x36 and a 1px dark outline separating it from the background. The outline and inset margin are what keep a relic legible when it is rendered over narrative dialogue art.
rules.title: Story relic silhouette framing

rules.summary: Portraits are 256x256 monochrome woodcut renders with hard black and white silhouette contrast. A full-colour or soft-shaded portrait breaks the unified print aesthetic the narrative layer is built on.
rules.title: Monochrome woodcut portrait style

rules.summary: Each story keyframe illustration is a 512x256 landscape plate in a 16:9 or 2:1 layout. A non-matching aspect ratio cannot be placed in the narrative panel without cropping the focal subject.
rules.title: Story keyframe aspect ratio

rules.summary: The regional map is a single 1920x1080 high-definition base sheet in a European parchment hand-charted nautical style. The fixed sheet size is what lets map markers address positions by stable coordinates.
rules.title: Frontier map base sheet

rules.summary: Three TrueType or OpenType font files must each cover the full 6763 simplified CJK glyph set of the GB2312 and GBK range, the complete ASCII range and full-width punctuation, and each is restricted to one role: display headline, body reading and terminal monospace. A partial glyph set renders as missing-glyph boxes, and one face reused for all three roles erases the size and rhythm hierarchy.
rules.title: Typography coverage and role split

rules.summary: All nineteen audio assets are Ogg Vorbis at a 44.1kHz sample rate and 16-bit depth with no clipping and no noise floor, inventoried across paper foley, UI interaction, impact and ambience. A clipping or off-spec asset is audible to the player as a defect regardless of how the game logic behaves.
rules.title: Audio fidelity and asset inventory

rules.summary: The art delivery contract requires each asset key to be snake_case and to match the name the code binds one to one. A key that diverges from its binding name leaves the asset unloaded while the engine falls back to a placeholder.
rules.title: Asset key binding to code

rules.summary: The art delivery acceptance checklist requires a texture placed on the #0F131A dark base to show no white fringe and no colour-fringed edges, and the delivery format is 32-bit PNG with a full alpha channel. Edge fringe is the most visible defect once the asset is composited onto the near-black UI surface.
rules.title: Alpha channel and edge cleanliness

rules.summary: Layering boundary breach in incremental pipeline (clean-layer semantics).
The project attribution section must name one project from the closed enumeration, so a commit can be routed to its owning project without prose parsing.
rules.title: 项目归属格式区与合法枚举校验

rules.summary: Commit messages are a long-lived technical record, so provisional or offhand wording such as wip, temporary, hack or placeholder must not stand in for an objective statement of what changed.
rules.title: 临时性与敷衍口吻词汇拦截

rules.summary: Absolute or promotional phrasing such as flawless, ultimate, bulletproof or 100% safe asserts a guarantee no test can establish, so a commit must state the mechanism and its verified coverage instead.
rules.title: 过度肯定与绝对化夸大表述拦截

rules.summary: Dismissive or emotional phrasing about prior work or other contributors belongs in review discussion, not in the permanent commit record, which must describe the change rather than judge it.
rules.title: 过度否定与情绪化贬损表述拦截

rules.summary: Slogans, marketing copy and narrative about the writing process describe intent rather than change, so a commit must name the affected behaviour or symbol instead.
rules.title: 风格元叙事、口号与宣传套话拦截

rules.summary: A step-by-step narration of the authoring session records how the work was produced rather than what the repository now contains, so the message must describe the resulting state.
rules.title: 程序化流水账与形式主义元叙事拦截

rules.summary: Execution-tag sections must not carry counts or scores, because a hand-written figure is a second source of truth that expires silently while the gate keeps passing.
rules.title: 执行标签区域零执行数字纪律

rules.summary: The commit subject must open with an imperative verb describing the change, so the subject reads as an instruction the repository now satisfies.
rules.title: 提交标题动词契约与祈使语态拦截

rules.summary: First-person and subjective narration attributes the change to a speaker rather than the code base, so the message must use impersonal, objective phrasing.
rules.title: 第一人称主观叙述与非客观人称拦截

rules.summary: Deeply nested inline callback chains create callback hell, complicate exceptionpropagation, and mask race conditions.
Dense syntactic packing of bitwise, arithmetic and conditional operators without namingor spacing exceeds human cognitive chunking capacity.
Giant expressions with deeply nested ternaries or unbounded logical chains createcognitive overload and obscure branching logic.
Cramming multiple distinct statements or side-effects onto a single line impairs stacktraces, debug stepping, and code readability.
Banner divider (═) used in small file (< 150 lines).
Async exported function lacks concurrency scheduling assumptions, reentrancy, or idempotence contract.
Public exported symbol lacks Docstring/JSDoc description, parameters, or return type documentation.
Tautological redundant comment merely repeating symbol or function name.
Source file missing top-level file header comment explaining responsibility and design intent.
Standard strict six-field file header missing one of six mandatory fields (Module, File Path, Architecture Role, Dependencies & Triggers, Responsibilities, Exit Semantics & Design Rationale).
File header declared path does not match actual physical file path.
File layout order violation: top-level six-field module header comment must precede all non-directive code statements.
Documented contract (pure, side-effect free, thread-safe) contradicts actual AST data flow or side effects.
Comment language deviates from dominant project or domain standard.
Unordered interleaving of languages in comments within a single file.
Encoding corruption detected (U+FFFD replacement characters, UTF-8 decoded as Latin-1, or Windows-1252 mojibake).
Inconsistent section separator styles mixed in same file (short ── title ── vs long ──── title).
Comment or docstring contains non-factual terminology, casual phrasing, hyperbolic assertions, or emotional slurs.
Low semantic comment density or verbatim line-by-line translation without explaining intent.
Comment or docstring physical line length exceeds 100 columns.
Multiple homogeneous unextracted literals (status codes, protocols, paths, events) in the same call scope should be clustered and extracted together.
Homogeneous semantic constants across files have naming splits or minor value drifts, violating single source of truth (SSOT).
Module-level constants must be placed in the primary declaration section immediately following imports, not scattered within functions or business logic.
Type definitions, interfaces, and contract shapes must be declared before core functions and business logic classes.
Large volumes of constants are scattered across business files without a structured, tiered constant library.
Shared constant ownership is misclassified; avoid dumping constants into kitchen-sink files or hiding them in private modules.
Local invariants, lazily initialized values, or short-lived resources must not be needlessly hoisted to module scope.
Multiple identical local literals in a function should be consolidated as local constants at the function header.
Complexity amplification trap: blocking I/O or serialization implicitly nested initeration or hot call chains.
Elastic complexity budget exceeded based on comprehensive language, role, scope, and clarity metrics.
Artificial splitting gaming: artificially deflating complexity by generatingexcessive single-line pass-through forwarding functions.
Uncontrolled complexity without architectural justification: high complexityoriginates from chaotic nesting and responsibility piling.
Uncontrolled deep control flow nesting: control flow nesting level exceeds elasticbudget for context type (business > 3, state machine > 5).
Deep long-span control flow escape: unstructured control flow escape(return/break/throw) executed in deep nesting (>= 4) far from function header.
Recursive or mutually recursive call chain without guaranteed termination guards across functions/files.
Distributed redundant complexity: highly similar algorithms, calculations, orvalidations scattered across multiple files creating latent complexity.
Unbounded transient memory allocation and repeated full materialization inside hot loops.
State machine dispatch structure standard: single branch within state machinebranches exceeds 30 LOC, degrading dispatch skeleton clarity.
Unbounded polynomial time complexity across function/file boundaries: nestediteration call chains incur prohibitive overhead.
Tautological loop traversal detected with zero or negligible state mutation entropy delta.
Redundant defensive validations within trusted internal domain boundaries.
Data access abstraction leak: business core directly manipulates persistence drivers or storage details.
N+1 query pattern and repeated storage calls within iteration or mapping contexts.
Unbounded data retrieval or full-table in-memory filtering in online request paths.
Resource registry bidirectional mapping inconsistency or dangling asset: resourcecenter contains empty paths or dangling references.
Repeated serialization and deserialization cycles across internal call chains.
Development-only dependency imported in production code: devDependencies package imported without type-only qualifier.
Dependency inversion violation: lower-level infrastructure or common modulesinversely depend on high-level business modules.
Function-scoped lazy import without audit declaration or documented rationale.
High-risk restrictive or viral copyleft license (AGPL/GPL) dependency introduced in proprietary/commercial domain.
Deprecated or unmaintained package imported: third-party library is officially unmaintained or superseded by standard capabilities.
File layout and import grouping do not conform to modern polyglot engineering standards.
File layout order violation: top-level import statement declared after contract types, constants, or business logic statements.
Import of undeclared external package (phantom dependency) not listed in project manifests (package.json, pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml).
Unpinned or wildcard dependency version: external package declared with floating wildcard (*, latest, open range) in project manifest.
Scattered hardcoded unmanaged external URLs, file paths, or connection strings in business logic.
Import of known-malicious, compromised, or severely vulnerable third-party package identified in supply chain integrity registry.
Wildcard import impairs explicit dependency tracking and tree-shaking optimization.
Declarative import boundary violation: cross-group dependency or unauthorized external package import.

rules.title: Internal jargon or math notation in release notes

rules.title: Engineering process wording in product release notes

Unclosed Markdown code fence detected.
Backtick path or relative link points to non-existent file.
README missing a required section anchor

rules.title: Released version absent from or stale in the README roadmap

rules.title: Roadmap summary citing fabricated settings or jargon

rules.summary: Documentation prose contains promotional slogans, hyperbolic claims, or unstandardized milestone jargon.
Identical literal frequency exceeds threshold in the same file (default >= 3 occurrences).
Unhandled floating promise: asynchronous operation executed without await, return, void, or .catch() error handler.
Vague or empty error diagnostic message: thrown error lacks actionable diagnostic context, root cause details, or troubleshooting hints.
Error code re-thrown across declarations or propagating through excessive call stack hops.
Expensive deep copy (.duplicate(true)) or blocking serialization/IO executed inside a loop.
File extension and directory classification guard: scripts must reside in dedicated domain subdirectories and never litter workspace root.
Myers diff, 3-way merge, Interval Tree O(log N + K) overlap query, and FastCDC chunking algorithm boundary and determinism guard
Cryptographic telemetry audit hash-chain guard: AuditRecord entries must stay <= 350 bytes with strictly monotonic Lamport clocks and verified HMAC-SHA256 signatures
Pre-review zone gate bridge verification guard: Strict rule catalog closure and sub-10ms AST slice check
Direct-Bypass test cache reclamation guard: Transient refs/taxis/test-cache entries must be physically reclaimed immediately after gate evaluation without leaking into canonical CAS
LayerVFS CAS snapshot materializer bridge: Fixed-time O(1) page cache mapping and atomic tree commit (advisory: no dedicated executable enforcer yet)
Core data model and error contract guard: Zero-panic Result propagation and immutable OID hashing semantics
Subsystem DAG single-direction dependency guard: Zero circular dependency and strict L1->L2->L3 layer isolation
Zero unwrap and expect panic guard: Enforce strong-typed Result propagation across production crates
Facade substantial burden and immutable freeze guard: Enforce substantial facade implementation with ELOC budget and deep object freezing (advisory: no dedicated executable enforcer yet)
Fractal Git domain gate guard: AST complexity constraints (CC <= 15), non-blocking I/O, and platform portability
Lockless in-memory git index concurrency guard: Conflict stage resolution, lock-free slot allocation, and deterministic read-tree/write-tree round-trip equivalence
Lock-free in-memory index concurrency guard: Prohibit blocking standard Mutex in virtual staging tree (advisory: no dedicated executable enforcer yet)

Commit header form guard: conventional type(scope) shape, unicode-character length bounds, trailing period, breaking marker, zero-width and hidden control characters, decorative emoji, and colon separator spacing
Commit section topology guard: semantic slot resolution with bilingual aliases, blank-line separation, duplicate rejection, topological ordering, and ASCII bracket and hyphen list markers
Commit body density guard: substantive character floors for production and non-critical types plus per-section floors for rationale, fix, and verification slots
Commit vocabulary guard: temporary and offhand wording rejected with word-boundary anchoring, inline code and URL masking, and the shared whitelist subtracted before the verdict
Commit unresolved marker guard: TODO, FIXME, TBD, XXX and Chinese deferred markers rejected together with unreplaced template angle-bracket placeholders
Commit empty section guard: a declared section carrying only a heading is rejected, and each change-list bullet must carry substantive content
Commit project scope guard: the project slot must exist, every declared name must match the controlled enumeration exactly, and non-standard project nomenclature is rejected
Commit batch codename guard: construction batch identifiers such as phase numbers, sprint numbers, pass numbers and week tokens are rejected as schedule vocabulary
Merge structure exemption guard: a generated merge message is exempted only when the commit object has two or more parents, never on header text alone
Commit declaration anchor guard: the verification slot must cite a symbol or test name that exists in the added lines of the staged diff
Commit policy tier guard: a command-line policy selector may tighten but never relax the tier declared by the versioned policy manifest
Commit rule identifier guard: every rule identifier quoted in a commit message must be registered in the single-source rule catalog
In-Kernel Canary Engine (IKCE) blind mutation kill rate guard: Candidate verification slice must achieve mutation kill rate K >= threshold with round-trip equivalence
Git object model serialization guard: Strict standard loose/pack object header format and SHA-1/SHA-256 dual compatibility
Resource recycling pool bounded governor: PathJail confinement, zero unbounded transient memory allocations, and deterministic lifecycle reclamation
Zero transient heap allocation guard in hot loops: Prohibit string, vector, and clone allocations in critical paths
Four-tier hierarchical audit rollup guard: Milestone card compression and periodic rollup must preserve Merkle root integrity and deterministic summary aggregation
Pre-Review Zone quarantine isolation and Bayesian credit circuit-breaker guard: Candidates failing kernel invariants or credit thresholds must be isolated into refs/taxis/quarantine
Documented unsafe block safety proof guard: Prohibit bare undocumented unsafe blocks in Rust crates
Storage layer crash safety: Append-only WAL journal consistency, loose ODB integrity, and CAS block deduplication
In-Kernel Canary Engine (IKCE) anti-tautology guard: Prohibit vacuous or tautological assertions (assert!(true), identical-operand equality) in verification slices
DAG topology traversal and Poset commutation guard: Cycle detection, ancestor generation indexing, and 3-way structural conflict detection
Smart HTTP transport and packet-line streaming framing protocol compliance and timeout guard
Taxis Kernel Code Verifier (TKCV) formal AST invariant guard: Enforce CFG soundness, handle lifecycle symmetry, parameter arity, and zero transient loop allocations

Staged commit batch envelope guard: one commit must stay inside a two-sided macro envelope of added and deleted logic and clear an empirical admission floor, because a batch too small carries no reviewable intent and a batch too large cannot be reviewed atomically

Staged single-file logic envelope guard: added and deleted effective logic per file must stay inside a two-sided envelope, because an unbounded add splits reviewable intent while an unbounded delete erases capability that no later gate can restore

Staged substantive density guard: the share of added physical lines that carry real logic, and the effective payload ratio of those same lines, must both sit inside a band with a floor and a ceiling, because a comment-heavy commit and a one-line stub are the same defect read from opposite ends

Staged differential exemption guard: an exemption may be granted only to a newly added short module whose mandatory module header cannot satisfy the density floor, only after a recorded streak of three blocks, only once per file, and never for batch overflow, capability erosion, or a payload ratio below its floor

Staged differential streak guard: repeated blocks of the same identifier must converge by recording the streak, announcing the pattern at the second failure, evaluating exemption at the third, and demanding explicit human acknowledgement at the fifth, because an undifferentiated block loop cannot be told apart from progress
Presentation layer directly manipulates bare ProgressBar instance, bypassing KStatusBar standard animations.
Presentation view directly couples with backend domain singletons or cross-layer global EventBus subscriptions.
Legacy Godot 3 signal connect signature passing method name as a string.
High-frequency UI button directly connected to signal without debounce mechanism or loading state lock.
Legacy Godot 3 export statement detected.
Presentation main view controller does not inherit from BaseScreen or BaseModal base class.
FSM private state variable mutated directly in-place, bypassing transition guards and lifecycle hooks.
Presentation UI text hardcodes raw strings without UIIntermediary or i18n translation key binding.
Headless domain logic layer directly references view layer or SceneTree nodes, breaking decoupled architecture.
